theater: 揚州廣陵城與淮水下游

battle.name: 廣陵之戰
battle.theater: 揚州廣陵城與淮水下游
battle.brief: 泰始五年（459年），北魏文成帝乘457年虎牢關失陷、淮北門戶洞開之勢，南下直取江淮重鎮廣陵，即劉宋揚州治所、江蘇揚州。宋軍依托古邗溝深溝高壘死守，魏軍久攻不克、糧道越拉越長，入冬前北退，江北屏障未破。卡面埃及長矛代表刺擊兵器的血脈：矛、槊與密排矛陣，兩軍攻守皆賴之。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方是北魏與劉宋。北魏都平城，文成帝拓跋浚自452年即位之後，鮮卑八部的騎兵仍是國家軍隊的骨幹，漢人郡縣兵、降附軍與各州鎮的戍兵補其步卒與守城之缺；調兵以大將軍、將軍為號，經尚書省與州鎮長官分派，糧秣則靠黃河、淮水一線的漕運與沿途屯田接濟。劉宋都建康，宋明帝劉彧以年號泰始在位，中樞由尚書省、中書省、門下省與領軍將軍、中軍將軍構成，揚州刺史鎮廣陵，豫州刺史鎮壽春，沿淮水與運河佈置重兵，並以水軍配合步卒守城。南北兩國在淮水一線長期拉鋒，多數時候各守據點、互不決戰，只在兵糧與渡口上互相牽制；泰始年間北魏連年用兵，才把這種僵持變成對廣陵的實圍。魏軍的戰力結構在南方並不佔優：騎兵在江南水網中行動受限，步卒與攻城工兵才是攻城的骨幹；而廣陵正是南朝唯一同時握有水軍、糧秣與城防三樣東西的城池，所以魏廷要打的不是一場會戰，而是一場以糧道與圍城為主的消耗戰。兩國的兵制體系也相差懸殊：魏以軍鎮屯田供軍，騎兵可以久屯於外而不動民財；宋則是兵、州、郡三級分領，州兵多為徵發的鄉兵，戰時集、散平時務農，一旦被圍在城內，便只能靠運河與徵糧續命。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were Northern Wei and the Liu Song dynasty. Northern Wei had its capital at Pingcheng, and after Emperor Wencheng, Tuoba Jun, took the throne in 452 the cavalry of the eight Xianbei tribal divisions remained the backbone of the state's army, while Han Chinese county troops, surrendered and defected formations, and the garrison soldiers of the various provincial towns filled in the infantry and the manning of the walls. Troops were dispatched under the titles of da jiangjun and jiangjun through the Shangshu Sheng and the provincial commanders, and grain was supplied by the Yellow River and the Huai River lines together with the fields cultivated by the frontier garrisons. Liu Song had its capital at Jiankang, and Emperor Ming of Song, Liu Yu, reigned under the Taishi era name; the central government was built from the Shangshu, Zhongshu and Menxia secretariats together with the Lingjun Jiangjun and the Zhongjun Jiangjun, while the Yangzhou governor held Guangling and the Yuzhou prefect held Shouchun, with heavy troops posted along the Huai River and the canal, and river troops cooperating with infantry in the defence of the walls. The two states had long jockeyed for position along the Huai, and for most of the time each held its own strongpoints without seeking a decision, competing only over grain and the fords. It was the repeated campaigning by Wei in the Taishi years that turned that stalemate into a real siege directed at Guangling. Wei's order of battle was not at its best in the south: cavalry was hampered by the water network of the Yangtze delta, and infantry with engineers for the assault was the real instrument of an attack. Guangling was the one city in the southern capitals that held river troops, grain and walls at the same time, so what Wei had come for was not a battle in the open but a war of consumption fought with supply lines and siege. The two military systems were also far apart: Wei supported its army from the tuntian of the military towns, so cavalry could stay in the field for months without draining the countryside; Song, by contrast, split its forces between the central troops, the provincial troops and the county troops, and much of the provincial soldiery was conscripted farmers who mustered for war and dispersed to farm in peace, so once they were shut up inside a wall they could be kept going only by the canal and by requisitioned grain.
people: 北魏文成帝拓跋浚在太武帝拓跋燾病殂的452年登基。太武帝一死，攝政的皇太子拓跋晃與幼弟拓跋余相繼在位，權臣乙渾把持朝政；453年乙渾被誅，拓跋浚才真正親政，此後他放還被幽禁的宗室、追尊父兄，逐步收回兵權，是一位以謹慎持國著稱的君主；太武帝450年南征至瓜步、無功而返的敗績，是魏廷始終想洗刷的舊帳。南面，劉宋明帝劉彧以猜忌聞名，即位後大誅宗室與前朝舊臣，邊防空虛反而讓北魏得到可乘之機；揚州刺史劉道濟出身劉宋宗室，自455年起鎮廣陵，是這場戰役中最關鍵一座城池的實際主官，直到466年劉子勛據廣陵起兵才被部下所害。同一時期宋的內部也在起火：皇族荊州刺史劉義宣455年舉兵反，457年兵敗被誅，國力與朝廷注意力都被牽制住；魏廷正是看準了這個空檔，才把兵鋒推過淮水。魏軍統兵大將的姓名在《宋書》《魏書》與《資治通鑑》之間記載參差，只能確定其位號是將軍、都督一類的方面統帥；同年降魏的宋將柳元景受封河陽侯，成為魏廷招降淮北州郡的樣板。南北兩廷的每一次進退，都是文武重臣在朝堂上反覆爭議的結果，而真正決定攻守節奏的，是能不能讓遠在後方的軍糧跟上城頭的消耗。
peopleEn: Emperor Wencheng of Northern Wei, Tuoba Jun, took the throne in 452 when Emperor Taiwu, Tuoba Tao, died of illness. After Taiwu's death the regent crown prince Tuoba Huang and his young brother Tuoba Yu sat on the throne in turn while the powerful general Yi Hun dominated the court; Yi Hun was killed in 453, and only then did Tuoba Jun really take charge, restoring the confined princes, honouring his father and elder brother and slowly taking back control of the army, and he is remembered as a careful ruler. The failure of Taiwu's advance to Guabu in 450, which achieved nothing, was the old humiliation the Wei court always wanted to wipe out. In the south, Emperor Ming of Song, Liu Yu, was famous for his mistrust, and after ascending the throne he put great numbers of the imperial clan and the previous court's ministers to death; the resulting vacancies in the frontier defences gave Wei its opportunity. Liu Daoji, the Yangzhou governor, came from the imperial clan of Liu Song and had held Guangling since 455, and he was the actual officer in command of the single most important city on the field in this campaign, and he was killed by his own men only in 466, when Liu Zixun rebelled at Guangling. Song was also aflame inside its own borders at this moment: the imperial clansman and Jingzhou governor Liu Yixuan rose in revolt in 455 and was destroyed in 457, which drained the state's strength and the court's attention alike; the Wei court had spotted exactly that gap before pushing its spearheads across the Huai. The names of the Wei commanders are recorded inconsistently in the Song Shu, the Wei Shu and the Zizhi Tongjian, and all that can be established is that they held the rank of jiangjun or dudu as area commanders. The Song general Liu Yuanjing, who surrendered in the same year, was made Marquis of Heyang and served as the model for the Wei court's efforts to win over the prefectures north of the Huai. Every advance and retreat on both sides was the result of argument between civil and military ministers at court, and what really set the tempo of the siege was whether the grain moving from the rear could keep pace with the consumption on the walls.
kits: 卡面上的兵器是埃及長矛，屬早王朝時期的形制：青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，用於守城垣與近身刺擊，是「木杆加金屬頭」這一刺擊兵器血脈的原型。經過青銅時代的數千年演替，銅矛先被鐵矛取代，再分化出長兵（槊）、兩刃的戟、帶喙的突擊兵器；到五世紀的江淮戰場，與它最接近的同類就是中原式的矛與槊。魏軍騎兵佩長槊，槊杆斜掛於馬鞍，衝鋒時用來對刺，步兵則以矛結陣；宋軍守城靠長矛與短兵相接，矛頭從城垛缺口伸出，專門迎擊攀城之敵。卡面沿用舊目錄的地域槽位標記，器物本身出自埃及早王朝。與之並用的還有弓、弩（守城用機弩、蹶張弩一類的張力裝置）、刀劍、盾，以及攻城用的撞車、雲梯、蒙衝與配重投石機；水軍有樓船與走舸，糧秣與攻城器械靠車隊與船隊，順著古邗溝與淮、泗水道北運。宋軍步兵多披札甲，即以小片皮甲綴聯成衣，胸前另加護心鏡；魏騎兵則靠馬具與皮甲自保，槊、刀與弓並列攜行，直到逼近城垣才把長兵換成撞車與雲梯。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is an Egyptian spear, of early dynastic type: a bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, used for the defence of walls and for thrusting at close quarters, and it is the archetype of the line of piercing weapons made as a wooden shaft plus a metal head. After several millennia of bronze-age substitution the bronze spear gave way to the iron spear, which then branched into the long spear or shao, the double-edged ji, and beak-headed thrusting weapons; on the Jiang-Huai battlefield of the fifth century the closest equivalents to the card were the plain Chinese spear and the shao. Wei cavalry carried the shao, its shaft slung along the saddle and used for the charge, while Wei infantry formed ranks with their spears; the Song relied on spears and short weapons on the walls, thrusting spearheads out through the gaps in the parapet to meet the men climbing up. The card keeps the regional slot marker used by the old catalogue, but the object itself comes from the early dynastic period in Egypt. Alongside it served bows, crossbows (with the tensioning devices of the powerful crossbow and the drawing crossbow on the walls), swords and knives, shields, and the assault equipment of the battering ram, the siege ladder, the covered ram and the counterweight stone-thrower; the river force had tower ships and light fast boats, and grain and siege equipment were moved north by wagon and by boat along the ancient Hangou canal and the Huai and Si waterways. Song infantry were commonly covered by lamellar armour, small plates of hide laced together into a coat with a separate plate over the chest, while Wei cavalry protected themselves with their harness and leather armour, carrying the shao, the sword and the bow together, and only swapped the long weapons for rams and ladders when they closed on the wall.
tactics: 北魏的戰法是把進攻拆成兩條腿：一條由騎兵沿淮水北岸與鄉里地帶掃掠郡縣、斷絕糧道、招降地方豪強，另一條由步卒與工兵跟著主力攻城，重點不在一日破城，而在先把外圍孤立起來，再對孤城施壓，等待援軍耗盡。廣陵城據古邗溝東端、北倚揚子江，進兵需先涉水或繞行，攻城器械在泥濘中運轉困難，魏軍因此屢屢受阻。宋軍的守禦是深溝高壘、閉門不出，牆頭密布弓弩與落石，長矛手列在垛口後方，專等攻城者登頭再刺；同時遣輕騎繞擊魏軍糧隊，又以水軍沿水路把援兵與糧食送進廣陵，把戰事拖成一場對耗。水軍小舟亦伺隙擾亂魏軍沿河的糧船，宋軍把援軍分成數批、以水路由淮入揚州，避免被魏騎在同一處一次吃掉；反過來，魏軍每次分兵劫掠，都等於把包圍圈往外拉長一圈。魏軍在圍城數月後被迫分兵劫掠，陣線拉長，騎兵因缺糧而疲，士氣與戰力同步下滑，最後在入冬前退回淮北。史家多以為，廣陵之戰的勝負不在一場會戰，而在誰能先把糧道維持得久。
tacticsEn: Wei's method was to split the attack in two: one arm of cavalry swept the districts north of the Huai and through the countryside, cutting the grain routes and winning over local magnates, while the other arm of infantry and engineers followed the main body to the walls. The point was not to take a city in a single day but to isolate the place first and then press the isolated city until the relief force was exhausted. Guangling stood at the eastern end of the ancient Hangou canal with the Yangtze to the north, so an attacking force had to ford water or detour, and siege engines were hard to move through the mud; Wei was blocked again and again for this reason. The Song defence was to dig deep ditches and raise high mounds, keep the gates shut and not sortie, pack the parapet with bows, crossbows and stones dropped from above, and station spearmen behind the crenellations waiting for the escaladers to show themselves; at the same time light cavalry went out to strike at the Wei supply columns, and river transports carried reinforcements and grain into Guangling by water, turning the campaign into a war of attrition. Small river boats also lay in wait to disturb Wei's grain boats along the waterway, and the Song brought their relief troops up in several separate bodies by water from the Huai into Yangzhou, so that the northern cavalry could not swallow them all in one place at once; conversely, every time Wei detached men to forage, it lengthened the ring of encirclement by a circle. After months of siege Wei was forced to send detachments far out to forage, its line of battle stretched thin, its cavalry weakened by short rations, and morale and fighting strength fell together, so the army withdrew north before winter. Most historians hold that the outcome of the battle at Guangling was decided not by any single engagement but by whoever could keep his supply line alive the longer.
data: 可用的數字不多，且多為概略之數。廣陵即今江蘇揚州，劉宋與南齊的揚州治所皆在此，扼揚子江北岸的古邗溝，向北可通淮、泗，向南距建康約二百三十公里，是江淮之間最短的水路要衝；魏軍自平城南下，經洛陽、汝、穎一路到廣陵，行程近兩千公里，因此遠征成敗極度依賴後方供應。戰役通常被繫於457至459年這一輪北魏南下，卡片取459年為其決定性年份，具體月份諸史記載參差，宜作約略理解，兩家史書都沒有留下可核的日數。《宋書》與《魏書》對魏軍兵數的記載從數萬到數十萬不等，後者顯係誇大，可靠的量級當在數萬；廣陵守軍則由揚州郡兵、徵發的丁壯與屯田兵組成，同樣是數千至數萬的量級。淮陰、盱眙、壽春等前沿據點在戰前都曾增兵，可知江淮防線是多點佈防而非孤城；魏軍南下多經許昌、汝南一路，說明它選的是最短的進軍軸線，而不是沿淮遊弋。圍城與拉鋒延續數季，魏軍北撤走的仍是原路，兩國邊線大致回到戰前位置。卡面兵器屬於前3200年前後的早王朝，距離459年已逾三千六百年，形制雖早，血脈未斷：槊與矛仍是五世紀戰場上最普及的刺擊兵器。
dataEn: Few reliable numbers survive, and most of them are approximate. Guangling is modern Yangzhou in Jiangsu; it was the seat of Yangzhou under both Liu Song and Southern Qi, it commanded the ancient Hangou canal on the north bank of the Yangtze, it could reach the Huai and the Si to the north, and it lay about 230 kilometres from Jiankang to the south, which made it the shortest water route between the river and the Huai. Wei's army, marching south from Pingcheng by way of Luoyang and the Ru and Ying valleys, covered close to two thousand kilometres, so the success of the expedition depended utterly on the supply system behind it. The campaign is usually attached to the round of Wei offensives between 457 and 459; the card takes 459 as its decisive year, while the precise month is recorded inconsistently and should be read approximately, since neither of the two histories preserves a verifiable day. The Song Shu and the Wei Shu give Wei's strength as anywhere from several tens of thousands to several hundred thousand, the latter plainly inflated, and a magnitude of some tens of thousands is the only defensible reading; the garrison at Guangling, drawn from the Yangzhou county troops, conscripted labour and the garrison farms, was on a scale of thousands to tens of thousands. The forward posts at Huaiyin, Xuyi and Shouchun all received reinforcements before the campaign, which shows that the line along the river was a chain of strongpoints rather than a single isolated city, and Wei's advance by the route through Xuchang and Runan shows that it had chosen the shortest axis of approach instead of ranging along the Huai. The siege and the standoff ran on for several seasons, Wei's withdrawal followed the line of its advance, and the border between the two states returned roughly to where it had been. The weapon on the card belongs to the early dynastic period of about 3200 BCE, more than 3,600 years before 459; its form is ancient but its lineage was unbroken, for the shao and the spear remained the commonest thrusting weapons on the fifth-century battlefield.
cause: 打起來有遠因，也有近因。遠因是北魏在太武帝晚年的內亂之後逐漸整頓戶籍、屯田與邊鎮，國力回升，文成帝一朝對南方的壓力重新變大；太武帝450年南征至瓜步、無功而返的舊敗，是魏廷想雪洗的恥辱，也是每一次南下的最深層動機。近因則在457年：北魏攻下虎牢關，宋方司州一線的門戶洞開，宋將柳元景等一批將吏降魏，淮北的人心與防線同時動搖；此後魏廷連年用兵，逐步蠶食淮南，終於把目光落在廣陵——只要拿下這座揚州治所，江北就再沒有可以擋住騎兵的堡壘，建康也直接暴露在淮水下游的威脅之下。劉宋方面的內部條件同樣脆弱：明帝大誅宗室與前朝大臣，宿將人人自危，州郡守令對北軍的進攻反應遲緩，軍費又因連年用兵而吃緊，朝廷在「出師北伐」與「固守待變」之間反覆爭議，終於採取了保守的守禦姿勢。宋廷內部同時還在「北伐」與「南渡自保」之間拉扯，明帝把兵權收在近臣與京師宿衛手中，州郡守令既無兵又無糧，遇北軍壓境只能退守請援；魏軍看準的正是這份空虛。北方要的是速戰速決，南方能做的只有拖延與外援。
causeEn: There were remote causes and immediate ones. The remote cause was that Northern Wei, after the disorders of the closing years of Emperor Taiwu, gradually reformed its registers, its tuntian and its frontier garrisons, so that its strength recovered and the pressure from the north became heavy again in the reign of Emperor Wencheng; the defeat of Taiwu's advance to Guabu in 450, which achieved nothing, was the humiliation the Wei court wanted to erase and the deepest motive behind every southern push. The immediate cause came in 457, when Wei took Hulao Pass, the Sizhou front of the Song stood wide open, a batch of Song officers including Liu Yuanjing went over to Wei, and the morale and the line of defence north of the Huai wavered together. Wei then campaigned year after year, eating away at the country south of the Huai piecemeal, until its eyes settled on Guangling: once that seat of Yangzhou fell, no fortress would remain north of the river to hold the cavalry, and Jiankang itself would be exposed to a threat coming down the lower Huai. Conditions inside Liu Song were just as weak. Emperor Ming had put the imperial clan and the previous court's ministers to death, serving generals lived in fear, the prefects and commandery governors reacted slowly to the northern advance, and years of war had strained the treasury. Court debate oscillated between striking north and holding fast, and the conservative course of defence was eventually adopted. Inside Song, argument also ran between striking out and simply drawing back behind the river, and the emperor concentrated authority in his close ministers and the garrison of the capital, so that the provincial commanders had neither men nor grain and could only fall back and ask for help when the northern army came on; that hollowness was exactly what Wei had come to exploit. The north wanted a quick decision; the south could only drag the fighting out and wait for help from outside.
impact: 這一仗沒有改變南北的基本格局，卻同時替兩邊留下了教訓。對北魏而言，廣陵城沒有拿下，意味著南進的腳步仍卡在淮水與運河交會處；遠征兩千公里的消耗、攻城器械的損耗與冬季的行軍，讓魏廷在文成帝與獻文帝兩朝把重心放回內部整頓——戶籍、屯田、邊鎮與宮殿工程都排在南征之前，直到孝文帝一朝重整軍備，攻勢才重新出現在長江北岸。此後數十年北魏未再大舉南征，直到孝文帝495年假道齊境、兵出河南義陽，才重新把戰火推回江淮；而劉宋正是在這段相對安寧中，把劉義宣之亂後殘存的軍力與府庫消耗殆盡。對劉宋而言，廣陵守住，等於揚州治所與建康之間的水路屏障得以延續，朝廷的重兵得以長期部署在江淮要衝；代價則是江南財政被北軍戰費長期拖累，軍鎮與州郡的依賴加深，為明帝末年與廢帝時期的急政埋下隱患。地理上，廣陵自此被坐實為「北控淮泗、南扼長江」的江淮樞紐，兩百多年後唐代把它經營成漕運總樞紐時，承載的正是同一條邗溝與同一個戰略位置。
impactEn: The battle changed nothing about the basic balance between north and south, but it left lessons on both sides. For Northern Wei, the failure to take Guangling meant the southern advance was still held up at the junction of the Huai and the canal. The cost of a two-thousand-kilometre expedition, the wear on the siege engines and the marching in winter pushed the Wei court, through the reigns of Wenchen and Xianwen, back towards internal reform, with registers, tuntian, the frontier garrisons and the palace works all placed ahead of any southern campaign; only after Emperor Xiaowen had rebuilt the army did the offensive reappear on the northern bank of the Yangtze. Wei did not attempt a large southern campaign again for several decades, and it was not until 495, under Xiaowen, that the army again came out through the territory of Qi into Henan and Yiyang and pushed the war back to the river; and Liu Song, in those comparatively quiet years, spent the last of the military force and the treasury that the revolt of Liu Yixuan had left it. For Liu Song, holding Guangling kept the water barrier between the seat of Yangzhou and Jiankang intact and allowed the heavy troops of the court to be stationed for the long term at the key point of the river. The price was a southern treasury drained by the cost of the northern war and a growing dependence on military commanders and provincial administrations, which fed the harsh government of the late Ming and the Feudi. Geographically, Guangling was now firmly fixed as the pivot of the river, controlling the Huai and the Si to the north and gripping the Yangtze to the south; when the Tang made it the great hub of grain transport two centuries later, it was the same Hangou canal and the same strategic position that were being used.
result: 結局是沒有結局：廣陵沒有陷落。魏軍久攻不克，糧秣不繼而退，北魏的南進第一次在江淮門戶前乾淨地停下，兩國的邊線大致回到戰前的樣子。這場戰役的實際收束並不是某一次會戰的勝負，而是補給：魏軍的糧道越拉越長，圍城的騎兵與步卒越來越依賴就地徵發，軍心與戰力同步下滑，最後在入冬前整軍北還；守方則靠深溝高壘與水運，把戰爭拖成對耗，靠援軍與糧船及時抵達撐住城頭。由於這場戰役在《宋書》《魏書》與《資治通鑑》裏的記載都很簡略，雙方將領姓名、兵數與戰場細節多有闕漏，戰爭表上所標的459年更像是取這一輪北魏南下的收尾年份，一般把457至459年的整段行動合稱為一役。它留下的最大遺產不是勝負，而是一條被反覆驗證的防線：只要揚州與建康之間的城防與水路不被突破，北方騎兵就無法把戰爭帶進江南的稻田與市鎮之間。從長時段看，這場未竟之役的真正收束係在二十年後：宋明帝死、廢帝即位，宗室相殘與朝政濁亂令北方每一次試探都更易得手，江淮防線的鬆動並非一日之失。
resultEn: The outcome was no outcome at all: Guangling did not fall. Wei's siege dragged on, its supplies failed to keep up, and it withdrew to the north, so Northern Wei's southward drive was checked cleanly for the first time at the gateway of the river, and the frontier between the two states returned roughly to its earlier shape. The campaign was not actually settled by the result of any single battle but by supply: Wei's grain route grew longer and longer, the besieging cavalry and infantry came to depend more and more on what they could requisition locally, and morale and fighting strength declined together until the army withdrew in good order before winter. The defenders, for their part, relied on deep ditches, high mounds and river transport to make the fighting a war of consumption, and on relief troops and grain boats reaching the walls in time to hold them. Because the records of this campaign in the Song Shu, the Wei Shu and the Zizhi Tongjian are all brief, with much missing about the commanders, the numbers and the details of the fighting, the year 459 given in the list of wars is better understood as the closing year of that round of Wei offensives, and the whole run of action from 457 to 459 is usually treated as a single campaign. Its greatest legacy is not a victory or a defeat but a defensive line that was tested again and again: as long as the walls and the water route between Yangzhou and Jiankang held, the northern cavalry could not carry the war into the paddy fields and market towns of the far south. In the longer run, the real closure of this unfinished campaign came two decades later: with the death of Emperor Ming of Song and the accession of the Feudi, the killing of princes within the clan and the murk of the court government made every northern probe easier, and the loosening of the line along the river was not the work of a single day.
